title: Scope channel WRITES to the caller's own project (membership) — default-deny cross-project posting

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: loopctl operator whose tenant has many projects and many agent keys
story.i_want_to: ensure an agent can only post to the channel of a project it belongs to — not any project in the tenant
story.so_that: one compromised agent key cannot inject prompt content into every project channel across the whole tenant

rationale: The security-adversary's prompt-injection blast-radius finding + signed-off decision 2: today the write only checks that the project is OWNED BY THE TENANT — post/3 calls Projects.get_project(tenant_id, project_id) (coordination.ex:154) and nothing more. So ANY tenant agent key can post to ANY project channel in the tenant, and that body auto-injects into every other session's SessionStart on that repo. One compromised agent key = a tenant-wide injector. Decision 2 makes the default 'the session's OWN repo/project channel, only that channel': the server must ENFORCE write-to-own-project (project-scoped keys / membership), default-deny cross-project posting — turning the client-side default into a real boundary against a rogue tenant key.

background.reference: signed-off decision 2 (membership = the session's own project; server enforces write-to-own-project); security-adversary 'Prompt-injection blast radius ... create only checks project ownership by tenant'; post/3 (coordination.ex:136-167, the check at :154); the existing ownership-rejected 422 path (channel_post_controller.ex:336-344).
background.includes: A project-membership (or project-scoped-key) predicate on the write path, default-deny, with the same oracle-safe 422 as the current cross-tenant rejection.

acceptance_criteria.description: The write (post/3, coordination.ex:136-167) authorizes the caller against the SPECIFIC project, not merely the tenant: the agent must be a member of / scoped to the target project. A post to a project the caller does not belong to (even within its own tenant) is rejected with the SAME byte-identical 422 ownership error the cross-tenant case already returns (@ownership_error_message, channel_post_controller.ex:74, 336-344) — no oracle distinguishing 'not a member' from 'not in your tenant' from 'does not exist'.

Membership is derived from an AUTHENTICATED, server-side source — either a project scope on the api_key (a project-scoped key) or an explicit membership relation — NEVER a client-supplied field. The exact mechanism is chosen from what loopctl already has (api_key project scoping if present; else a minimal channel-membership predicate); the choice + its source table are documented. Default-DENY: absent an explicit membership/scope, the write is rejected.

The READ posture is unchanged (reads stay oracle-safe + tenant-scoped as today, channel_post_controller.ex:200-254) — this story scopes WRITES only. A test asserts a second project in the SAME tenant, that the agent is not a member of, cannot be posted to, while the agent's own project still works.

If a full membership model is out of reach in this story, the accepted-risk fallback (re-scope line 98 / decision 2) is per-project-scoped agent keys as the compensating control — but that must be a DELIBERATE, documented sign-off, not a silent no-op. Default remains deny cross-project; the story does NOT ship leaving the tenant-wide hole open. The security signal (:ownership_rejected, channel_post_controller.ex:338) fires on a cross-project attempt so the injector is observable.

test_cases.name: agent posts to its own project
preconditions: agent A scoped/member of project P1

test_cases.name: agent cannot post to a sibling project in the same tenant
preconditions: project P2 in the same tenant; agent A not a member of P2
expected_results: 422 @ownership_error_message (byte-identical to cross-tenant); :ownership_rejected signal fires; nothing persisted

technical_notes: The check lives in post/3 (coordination.ex:154): today `with {:ok, _project} <- Projects.get_project(tenant_id, project_id)`. ADD a membership predicate: `... , {:ok, _} <- project_writable_by_agent(tenant_id, agent_id, project_id)` returning {:error, :not_found} on non-membership so the endpoint maps it to the SAME 422 (channel_post_controller.ex:336-344) — no new error code, no oracle.

FIRST establish what loopctl has: does api_keys carry a project scope? Is there an agents<->projects membership relation? Grep for project scoping on api_key / a project_members-style table. Use the existing mechanism; only add a minimal one if none exists. Document the source in the story impl.

Also gate the CLAIM writes (40.B1 claim/release/done) and the graduate (40.E1) the same way — a claim/graduate on a project you cannot post to should also be denied. Note the coupling; keep the predicate shared.
Keep the :ownership_rejected telemetry (channel_post_controller.ex:336-344) firing so a cross-project attempt is observable (AC-39.2.9 parity).

Decision 2 fallback (per-project-scoped keys as the compensating control) is acceptable ONLY as a documented sign-off (AC-40.D3.4) — never ship silently leaving any tenant agent able to post anywhere.
